name: timecode-field
title: Timecode field
description: Edits hours, minutes, seconds, and frames with native form validation for a supplied integer non-drop frame rate.
docs: Vlak leaves are StyleX. Compile them with @stylexjs/babel-plugin (Vite: @stylexjs/unplugin, Next: @stylexjs/nextjs-plugin). If you would rather not run a compiler, import @noorddev/vlak-react instead: it ships precompiled with one stylesheet.

vlak.snippet: 24 fps, non-drop. Hours:minutes:seconds:frames.
vlak.example:
import { TimecodeField } from "@noorddev/vlak-react";

<TimecodeField label="In point" name="inPoint" frameRate={24} defaultValue="00:01:24:12" required />

use: Integer non-drop rates from 1 through 99, supplied explicitly by the application.
Two-digit hours, minutes, seconds, and frames separated by colons.
onValueChange receives editable text, including incomplete input; check native validity before committing.
avoid: Drop-frame, fractional frame rates, or automatic conversion between timecode standards.
Coercing invalid frame numbers into a different timestamp without user intent.

keyboard.does: Edits and selects timecode text using native input behavior.

a11y: A visible label names the input, and the frame-rate hint or validation error is linked as its description.
The format pattern and custom validity reject out-of-range frames and unsupported rates; required uses native form validation.
A 44px input target and focus ring accompany aria-invalid on invalid timecode.
The ref and native input attributes reach the input; uncontrolled form reset restores the default text.
